harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 as the internal NTP time source for the cluster and node2 to sync exclusively against node1, then verified persistence and recovery across a rolling restart of both nodes.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline chrony config/state on both nodes (both RHEL 9.8, chrony 4.8, synced to public pool, stratum 3)
On node1: added 'allow 10.100.90.11/32' and 'local stratum 10' to /etc/chrony.conf so it serves time even without upstream sync; backed up original config
Opened firewalld NTP service (123/udp) permanently on node1
Restarted chronyd on node1 to apply config
On node2: removed the public 'pool 2.rhel.pool.ntp.org iburst' line and added 'server 10.100.90.10 iburst prefer' pointing at node1; backed up original config
Confirmed /run/chrony-dhcp had no DHCP-supplied NTP sources that could conflict
Restarted chronyd on node2 and verified it synced exclusively to node1 (Reference ID 0A645A0A = 10.100.90.10, state '*', Leap status Normal)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline for both nodes

Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect), polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, verified chronyd active, config persisted (allow/local stratum), firewall rule persisted, and pool re-sync succeeded

Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, verified chronyd active, config persisted (server-only, no pool), and re-sync to node1 achieved (stratum 4, current best source, Normal)
Final check: node1 chronyd active and shows node2 as an active NTP client

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as internal time source (baseline)
evidence.summary: node1 baseline: RHEL9, chrony active, default public pool config, tracking synced stratum 3 Normal

evidence.requirement: node1 chrony.conf updated to allow node2 and serve as authoritative local source
evidence.summary: Added 'allow 10.100.90.11/32' and 'local stratum 10' to node1 chrony.conf, restarted chronyd, opened firewalld ntp service permanently

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to sync against node1 instead of public server
evidence.summary: Removed pool line, added 'server 10.100.90.10 iburst prefer' to node2 chrony.conf, restarted chronyd; chronyc sources/tracking show node2 synced to Reference ID 0A645A0A (node1's IP), Leap status Normal

evidence.requirement: node1 actively serving node2 as NTP client
evidence.summary: chronyc clients on node1 lists node2's hostname with nonzero NTP request count, both before and after the restart sequence

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 98aa35f5...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id changed to 4c4fee11...; chronyd active with allow/local-stratum config intact; re-synced to public pool (stratum 3, Normal) confirming service recovery

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state (still syncing to node1 only)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 6bb7e004...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id changed to dbe95813...; chronyd active with server-only (node1) config intact, no public pool; re-synced to node1 as current best source (Reference ID 0A645A0A, Leap status Normal)

evidence.requirement: node2 not disrupted while node1 was rebooting (independent recovery path / no double outage)
evidence.summary: During node1's reboot window, node2 remained active with prior tracking data (Leap status Normal), confirming only one node was down at a time

attempts.summary: Configured node1 as the internal NTP time source for the cluster and node2 to sync exclusively against node1, then verified persistence and recovery across a rolling restart of both nodes.
